name: Nagoya robot
full_name: Nagoya University catheter-driving robots for intravascular neurosurgery (roller and linear-stepping drives) with the EVE patient-specific simulator
group: Nagoya University (Toshio Fukuda, Fumihito Arai; neurosurgeon Makoto Negoro), later Seiichi Ikeda and Carlos Tercero
versions: 1996 ICRA networked telesurgery over optical fibre (arai1996_multimedia, doi:10.1109/ROBOT.1996.503883, title via dblp; cited as ref. 1 of tanimoto2000); 2000 MICCAI telesurgery system (tanimoto2000_telesurgery, full): 2-DOF roller slave whose outer shell turns for rotation, inner unit hung on strain-gauge beams (2-axis force), slave 'first designed in 1994' (Fig. 3), wire-driven 2-DOF master joystick (1.6 um, 0.023 deg encoders), 1.2 x 5 mm tip micro force sensor (0.5 mN, 2 kHz), in vitro telesurgery in an intravascular operating room with the doctor 5 m away watching X-ray (Sec. 3, 5); 2001 robotic controlled catheter system with motorized roller feeding (Negoro et al., via miyachi2025_robotics Fig. 1 and text); 2002 linear-stepping slave ('mechanical pencil' mechanism): two grasping units knocked by voice-coil motors, DC-motor rotation of the grasped catheter, voice-coil brake, disposable grasping unit, tip micro force sensor and force-feedback master joystick designed (arai2002_new, full; it replaces the 2000 roller slave, which slipped and was hard to sterilise); 2006 patient-specific neurovascular simulator EVE for evaluating robots (ikeda2006_patientspecific, title); 2007 IJMRCAS autonomous catheter insertion with magnetic motion capture (tercero2007_autonomous, full): the 2002 linear-stepping mechanism rebuilt as a stand-alone unit with a microcontroller, 2 DOF (insert/extract at variable speed, twist in one direction), steered by an NDI Aurora 0.8 x 8 mm coil (Sec. Catheter insertion mechanism, Fig. 2a); 2010 catheter insertion robot with photoelastic stress visualisation (ikeda2010_threedimensional, title)
devices_driven: catheter (4 Fr, 1.35 mm, in the 2002 tests; arai2002 Sec. 3)
n_dof_detail: 2 (forward/backward and rotation) for the 2002 slave (arai2002 Sec. 2.1)
translation_detail: friction-roller (2000-2001 roller feeding; arai2002 Sec. 1: when the vessel's resistance exceeds the pushing force, the roller slips); 2002 linear-stepping slave: two grasping units knocked by voice-coil motors, a brake holds the catheter between strokes (clamp-relay type; arai2002 Sec. 2.2)
rotation_detail: 2002: a DC motor (Table 1: 12 V, gear ratio 22:1) turns the grasping unit while it holds the catheter (arai2002 Sec. 2.2)
device_range: 4 Fr catheter in the tests; step per cycle settable from 1 to 10 mm (arai2002 Sec. 3)
footprint_mm: 2002 slave about 300 mm long (arai2002 Sec. 2.3: "about 30cm"); other dimensions N.R.
force_sensing: 2002: a micro force sensor at the catheter tip measures the catheter-vessel contact force for force feedback and the brake (arai2002 Sec. 2.3; no force data reported); none in the drive itself (he2018_linear Introduction); photoelastic stress in the phantom used to visualise wall stress (2010, title); 2000 roller slave: strain gauges on thin beams measure push and rotation reaction forces, plus a 1.2 mm x 5 mm tip micro force sensor (resolution 0.5 mN, 2 kHz) displayed together on the master (tanimoto2000 Sec. 3.2-4.1)
haptics_leader: 2002: master joystick with force feedback designed (arai2002 Sec. 2.3, Fig. 10); not evaluated; 2000: 2-DOF force-reflecting master joystick (prismatic + revolute, wire-driven, no gears) with variable-impedance and multi-sensor force display (tanimoto2000 Sec. 3.1, 4)
imaging_compat: 2000: in vitro telesurgery under the X-ray camera of an intravascular operating room, master in the next room (tanimoto2000 Sec. 5, Fig. 11); 2007: NDI Aurora magnetic motion capture (tercero2007)
sterility: 2002: disposable grasping unit and brake contact part (arai2002 Sec. 2.1, 2.2); the earlier roller slave was not suitable for sterilisation (arai2002 Sec. 1)
validation_detail: in vitro patient-specific membranous silicone cerebral artery models (EVE) (ikeda2006_patientspecific, title-level); clinical use N.R.; 2001 system 'quite large', forward/backward only, not practical (miyachi2025_robotics) 2002 slave: bench only, catheter driven forward, backward and in rotation with the tip in a 5 mm pipe, distance by optical encoder (arai2002 Sec. 3, Figs. 12-18). 2000: in vitro telesurgery, soft plastic tube vessel model under X-ray in the intravascular operating room (tanimoto2000 Sec. 5). 2007: autonomous insertion in silicone block and membranous models of the aortic arch and carotids, speed control and 1-D / 2-D path reconstruction (tercero2007).
key_numbers: 2002 slave: brake holding force about 220 gf, adjustable 0-300 gf (arai2002 Sec. 2.2); with the step set to 1 mm the measured step was 0.3-1.9 mm, so the stroke was "not stable" (Sec. 4, Fig. 18); slower than a roller drive (Sec. 2.1). Other papers not read. 2007: catheter speed controlled at 6.14 mm/s; 2-D path reproduced with < 7 mm error (tercero2007 Abstract).
sim_model: physical in vitro simulator (EVE), not a computational model; EVE phantoms are reused by later robot studies (e.g. A2 southeast_jin2024)
